correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, constrained H^2 minimization gives q_n=(1/m)sum_{j=0}^{m-2}(m-1-j)z^j, m=n+2, with unique equality. Exact identity m(1-z)^2 q_n=z^m-mz+m-1 reduces roots to (1+w)^m=1+mw. For Re w>=|Im w|, strict binomial modulus growth contradicts the equation, including boundary. F_m=q_n(1+w/m)/m converges locally uniformly to (exp(w)-1-w)/w^2, with F(0)=1/2. Rouche/implicit-function arguments give all bounded-domain root counts and the w_0(1+w_0)/(2m) correction. 38 exact algebraic checks, 16 finite root tests, and 5 high-precision tracking tests passed; finite checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The 2021 survey asks explicitly whether sectors based at a unit-circle boundary point exclude all zeros of optimal polynomial approximants. The canonical function 1-z is the first natural singular test case; a degree-uniform outward cone and its complete inverse-degree zero process provide new geometric understanding, with a two-term asymptotic linking the otherwise qualitative zero repulsion to exact Lambert-W values. This is a natural self-contained analytic result, not merely a finite computation; broader generality and sharp cone width are not claimed.
